claims.text: The target material is a solid-solution high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 atomic percent each.
Superconducting behavior in the target alloy is governed by the combination of high configurational entropy and clustered ordering.
Localized pockets of nonrandom atomic distributions are also called clustered ordering.
Solid-solution high-entropy alloys can contain localized nonrandom atomic distributions.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution.
Clustered ordering increases the superconducting critical temperature.
Clustered ordering increases the superconducting upper critical field.
The predicted enhancement is relative to conventional superconducting alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies generally to high-entropy alloys having at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
The exact relationship among configurational entropy, clustered ordering, and superconducting properties is not fully understood.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% increase in critical temperature or upper critical field as clustered ordering increases would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is specified as conventional superconducting alloys, whereas the requested starting material is the high-entropy alloy and the falsification design instead compares different levels of ordering within an HEA. These fields do not define a consistent controlled comparator.
